parts: A statement is a sentence that is either true or false, not both. Commands, questions and opinions are not statements.
~p is true when p is false. 'All A are B' is negated as 'Some A are not B' (or 'Not all A are B'); 'x < 5' as 'x is not less than 5'.
p ∧ q (and) is true only when both are true; p ∨ q (or) is false only when both are false. 'p if and only if q' (p ⇔ q) means both p ⇒ q and q ⇒ p.
Converse: if q then p. Inverse: if not p then not q. Contrapositive: if not q then not p. A statement and its contrapositive are equivalent; the converse need not be true.
'It never rains when it is cold' becomes 'If it is cold, then it never rains'. 'p if q' means 'if q then p'.
By direct method, contrapositive, contradiction, or a counterexample to show a statement false.
